correctness.rationale: The claim fixes odd q=p^e>=3 and additive G=F_q^2 with H={(t,t^-1): t≠0}, g=1_H and ALL time-frequency measurements. For h=(a,b)=H−H, solve t²−at+a/b=0; h=0 overlap q−1 and nonzero overlaps 1+χ(1−4/(ab)) in {1,2}, giving |D|=1+(q−1)^2/2. Any ambiguity coefficient with h in D sums m(h)=1,2,q−1 many pth roots; irreducibility of Φ_p forces all residue counts equal if zero and hence p|m(h), impossible, so ALL frequencies nonzero on D. Time/modulation Fourier transforms of the lifted spectrogram isolate each lag and multiply by its ambiguity coefficient; therefore rank_C L_g=q²|D|, kernel precisely matrices on unobserved lags. Rank-one data recover all moduli and edge-relative phases, yielding phase torus of dimension c−1 on support graph. At q=3, D is diagonal subgroup with three cosets; for q>=5, varying t with fixed nonzero first coordinate creates a vertical difference, multiplicative dilation fills vertical axis and hence G, proving full-support connectivity. Independently generated H, D, discriminant multiplicities, all-modulation cyclotomic multiplicity constraints, and Cayley connectivity for prime q=3,5,7,11,13,17; recovered D=3,9,19,51,73,129, lifted ranks 27,225,931,6171,12337,37281, components 3,1,1,1,1,1. Proof explicitly includes nonprime odd prime powers; finite prime tests only corroborate that universal algebra.

value.rationale: The inverse-graph hyperbola is a natural sparse aperture for finite-field STFT. Exact operator-lifting rank and kernel, all pure-state phase fibers, and the surprising q3/q5 full-support connectivity threshold quantify precisely what such highly rank-deficient measurements can recover. They complement known hyperbola Fourier moments and generic phase graph propagation, giving natural useful invariants for every odd finite field.
